$comment: The area registry (docs/test-explorer-spec.md §5, amended by §2a/§2c). Rows are feature areas in product language, matching the outer `describe` convention in testing-strategy.md §9.1 - undotted, not an entity ('Triage', not 'item.setStatus'). A source file can legitimately match more than one area's sourcePatterns (e.g. apps/api/src/domain/items.ts backs Capture, Triage and Offline as different functions in one file) - that is expected, not an overlap error. `pnpm --filter @cockpit/test-explorer check-concepts` instead fails when a test declares an area missing from this file. A file matching zero areas falls into 'infrastructure' automatically. Concepts with an empty sourcePatterns list are declared ahead of the code that will eventually own them and stay at zero everywhere until then. Glob syntax: '*' within a path segment, '**' across segments. The nine areas below are testing-strategy.md §9.1's own example list verbatim. An entry can carry an optional "parent": "<key>" naming another entry's key, turning the flat list into a tree - a real feature area that's grown too big for one row (Dashboards is the expected first case: drag-drop, resizing, ...) gets children this way rather than being renamed in every test that already uses it. No entry needs one yet, since nothing here has grown a real sub-area in tests - add the field the day one does, matching whatever the actual describe names in those tests turn out to be, not a guess made ahead of the code the way the empty-sourcePatterns entries below are.
